project: Engine Renderer Editor Responsibility Split And Command/Toml Unification
goal: Restructure the application so Engine owns runtime system ticking, Renderer owns renderer-specific config UI registration, Editor becomes the top-level assembly/bootstrap product, all existing ini-based configuration paths are replaced by toml-based paths, and the command line model becomes slash-command plus default-cvar semantics with centralized helper metadata.

checkpoints.title: Freeze the top-level ownership split
checkpoints.problem: Engine, Renderer, Editor, Console, and EditorUI are still connected through mixed hooks and editor-owned orchestration. The current boundary is muddy: Engine owns renderer lifetime but Editor still owns Console and UI assembly while Renderer also participates in frame orchestration.
must_be_true_after: Editor is only the assembly/bootstrap product. It decides startup parameters, startup config sources, window/UI bootstrap inputs, and initial asset presets, then launches Engine with those inputs.
Engine owns runtime system lifetime and frame ticking order for runtime-facing systems, including Console, UI host, command processor, renderer, and other runtime subsystems.
Renderer is no longer treated as a pseudo-app coordinator. It only owns rendering behavior plus renderer-specific config UI registration and data exposure.
Renderer selection and switching are still initiated by the top-level runtime flow, but the runtime flow lives in Engine rather than editor-side ad-hoc composition.
tasks: Define one explicit startup contract from Editor to Engine, likely an EngineStartupConfig or equivalent, covering window options, UI bootstrap options, initial asset/config paths, and renderer default selection.
Move Console construction and runtime system ownership under Engine so Editor no longer owns runtime subsystems directly.
Replace generic EngineHooks drift with narrower responsibilities: runtime tick orchestration belongs to Engine, renderer callbacks belong to rendering concerns only.
Delete hook paths that only exist because Editor currently stitches runtime systems together manually.

checkpoints.title: Move config UI ownership to Renderer and partition Configs by renderer
checkpoints.problem: Configs currently mixes generic editor controls and renderer-specific controls through editor-side knowledge of raster/raytracing sub UIs. This leaks renderer detail into EditorUI and makes renderer switching a UI ownership problem instead of a renderer registration problem.
must_be_true_after: Renderer registers its config UI sections into the shared Configs window through one engine-owned/UI-owned registration interface.
Configs window is partitioned by renderer, so common runtime/editor sections and renderer-specific sections are visually and structurally separate.
EditorUI no longer hardcodes renderer-specific UI classes as primary owners of config composition.
Changing renderer no longer requires editor-side branching over raster/raytracing config widgets as the main composition model.
tasks: Define a renderer config panel registration contract with explicit section naming and lifetime rules.
Move raster/raytracing config panel registration out of EditorUI branching and into renderer-owned registration on startup/switch.
Keep shared editor/runtime panels in the central UI host, but renderer partitions come from renderer registration only.
Delete transitional editor-side renderer UI dispatch after the new partition model lands.

checkpoints.title: Replace all ini-based startup/config flows with toml
checkpoints.problem: The runtime still mixes toml with multiple ini paths: ConsoleVariable.ini, imgui.ini, preset_imgui.ini, and direct ini-related code in ConfigManager. This breaks the desired latest-only configuration model and leaves startup behavior split across incompatible formats.
must_be_true_after: All application-owned startup and persisted config flows use toml only.
Console variable overrides are loaded from toml, not ConsoleVariable.ini.
ImGui layout/preset persistence no longer depends on imgui.ini or preset_imgui.ini as external ini files.
All application-side ini-specific loading code is deleted, including the direct ConfigManager ini include and the ConsoleVariable.ini copy/install path.
tasks: Define where cvar override data lives in toml, likely under an explicit engine/editor cvar table with string-preserving semantics.
Replace CVar::ApplyIniFile with a toml-driven apply path instead of adding a parallel compatibility loader.

Replace imgui.ini file persistence with explicit SaveIniSettingsToMemory / LoadIniSettingsFromMemory style integration stored in toml-owned text or an equivalent toml-backed field, so the runtime still uses ImGui layout data without external ini files.
Update build/resource copy rules so no .ini file is required or copied for runtime startup.

checkpoints.title: Delete ini-only dependencies and dead paths
checkpoints.problem: Even after moving app config to toml, dead ini code and dependencies can linger in the tree and build graph. That keeps the wrong ownership model alive and invites regressions.
must_be_true_after: There is no app-owned runtime path that requires or copies a .ini file for startup or persistent editor state.
Dead ConsoleVariable.ini logic is removed instead of retained as fallback compatibility.
The app-side ini helper / third-party ini parsing dependency used only for this legacy path is removed from includes and from the relevant build graph.
Template and root config docs describe toml only.
tasks: Delete ConsoleVariable.ini and its copy/install expectations after toml replacement lands.
Delete or stop including config/ini.h from ConfigManager once no ini flow remains.
Audit source and docs for .ini references and remove app-owned leftovers instead of documenting them as legacy behavior.
Keep only third-party internal ini usage that is truly external-library-owned and unavoidable; app-owned ini persistence must be gone.

checkpoints.title: Redesign command semantics around slash commands and default cvars
checkpoints.problem: The current text command processor treats all text uniformly and still carries console-era parsing assumptions. The desired model is mode-based: leading `/` means engine command, otherwise text is interpreted as a cvar operation by default.
must_be_true_after: Any input beginning with `/` is interpreted as an engine command.
Any input not beginning with `/` is interpreted as a cvar expression by default.
Appending `?` to either a command or a cvar prints helper text instead of executing mutation logic.
Helper text is declared with the command/cvar definition and not hand-authored in console-specific parsing code.
tasks: Define a command declaration model that stores name, helper text, parse/execute callback, and candidate text in the processor-owned registry.
Normalize cvar query/mutation grammar so `Name ?` prints helper and current state while `Name value` mutates, with no separate legacy grammar path.
Decide whether slash commands use flat names or hierarchical paths, but keep one canonical syntax only.
Delete any console-local command knowledge once the processor-owned slash/default-cvar model lands.

checkpoints.title: Unify candidate/help metadata and scrollable command completion UI
checkpoints.problem: Autocomplete currently depends on console-side string probing and cvar enumeration. That model cannot express slash-command candidates cleanly, and it keeps helper/candidate metadata split between processor and UI.
must_be_true_after: Console completion candidates come from one processor-owned query surface that returns both slash commands and cvar candidates according to the current parse mode.
The candidate list remains scrollable and selection-capable in the console UI.
Helper text and completion text come from the same declaration metadata used for execution.
Console UI does not need to know command semantics beyond candidate rendering and line submission.
tasks: Add a processor-owned candidate query API with read-only visitation instead of returning cross-module STL containers by value.
Split slash-mode candidate rules from default-cvar-mode candidate rules inside the processor.
Keep console-side scroll/select behavior, but drive the content from processor metadata.
Make helper text retrieval a first-class processor query path so `?` output is not reconstructed in UI code.

checkpoints.title: Rebuild frame orchestration around Engine-owned runtime ticking
checkpoints.problem: Even after the command processor landed, the broader frame loop still uses renderer hooks in a way that hides actual runtime ownership. To satisfy the target design, Engine must become the single owner of runtime tick order while Renderer remains one participant in that sequence.
must_be_true_after: Engine has one explicit runtime tick phase ordering for UI host, command processing, console, renderer-facing UI registration, scene/runtime subsystems, and renderer frame execution.
Renderer frame execution is called by Engine as one runtime step, not treated as the owner of unrelated runtime orchestration.
Console and other runtime systems are no longer stitched through editor-only overlay composition as their primary ownership path.
The frame loop is easier to reason about because runtime ownership order exists in one place instead of being split between Editor, Engine, and renderer hooks.
tasks: Define the final per-frame order explicitly in Engine: window/context tick, runtime UI/input capture, command processing, runtime subsystem ticks, renderer config registration sync, renderer frame execution, present/platform windows.
Reduce renderer hooks to rendering-relevant integration points only.
Move runtime system construction and destruction out of Editor and into Engine where they are part of runtime ownership.
Keep Editor focused on startup assembly, not per-frame runtime composition.

milestones.title: Ownership split first
milestones.why: Without freezing Engine/Renderer/Editor ownership, later command/config work will keep leaking across layers.

milestones.title: Toml-only config migration
milestones.why: All startup and persisted state must converge before command/config UX can be considered final.

milestones.title: Command model and console UX
milestones.why: Slash-command semantics, default cvar fallback, helper text, and scrollable candidates should land on top of the new ownership and config model, not before it.

design_notes.engine_boundary: Engine should own runtime object lifetime and frame tick ordering. If a system exists every frame and affects runtime/editor state, it belongs under Engine ownership rather than Editor-side assembly after startup.
design_notes.renderer_boundary: Renderer owns rendering behavior and renderer-specific config panel registration only. It should not own generic runtime systems or generic editor composition.
design_notes.editor_boundary: Editor is the executable/bootstrap layer. It builds startup config, resolves startup files, selects initial bootstrap assets/window/UI choices, and launches Engine. It should not remain the long-term owner of runtime systems.
design_notes.toml_migration_rule: Do not keep ini fallback. Replace app-owned ini flows with toml and delete ini paths after migration.
design_notes.command_rule: `/` means command. No `/` means default cvar expression. `?` always means helper/output query using declaration metadata.
design_notes.imgui_layout_rule: If ImGui still needs ini-formatted layout text internally, keep the format in memory only and persist it through toml-owned storage. External .ini files must disappear from app-owned runtime behavior.

risks: If Engine/Renderer/Editor ownership is not frozen first, command and config refactors will continue to leak responsibilities across modules.
Removing imgui.ini without a clear in-memory persistence replacement can accidentally wipe docking/layout persistence.
Mixing slash commands and default cvar parsing without one canonical grammar will recreate console-specific special cases.
Keeping any ini fallback path will weaken the migration and preserve dead config branches indefinitely.
